# Crossing Persia

> Crossing Persia (https://www.crossingpersia.com) is a travel diary told one day at a
> time. A traveller named Arion sets out from Athens on 17 November 500 BCE and
> walks toward the Persian Empire. One new day is published each real day, starting
> on 17 November 2026, so Day 1 of the diary matches 17 November 2026 and Day 2 matches
> 18 November 2026. Days after the current date are not shown.

Arion is a fictional narrator. The places, roads, objects and customs in each day are
drawn from historical and archaeological sources, which are listed at the end of that
day under "Based on evidence". Each day has a picture with its caption and photo credit.

Each day can be read in English, in Dari (the Persian spoken in Afghanistan, written
as spoken in Kabul) and in Kurmanji Kurdish. The Dari version has a recording and lets
the reader tap any word for its meaning.

## Main sections

- [Cover](https://www.crossingpersia.com/): today's date in 500 BCE and the day of the journey
- [Travel Journal](https://www.crossingpersia.com/journal.html): every published day,
  one card per day with its picture, grouped by week
- [Day pages](https://www.crossingpersia.com/day-1.html): one page per day, with the
  full English story, the picture's caption and the sources written into the page.
  Change the number for another day (day-2.html, day-3.html ...). The Dari and Kurmanji
  versions are at day.html?day=1&lang=fa and day.html?day=1&lang=kmr, filled in by JavaScript.
- [Maps](https://www.crossingpersia.com/maps.html): Arion's route so far, day by day
- [Map Sources](https://www.crossingpersia.com/map-sources.html): every source used to
  draw the route map
- [About the Project](https://www.crossingpersia.com/about.html): why the diary exists,
  in English, Dari and Kurmanji
- [Substack](https://crossingpersia.substack.com/): the project's posts
- [Sitemap](https://www.crossingpersia.com/sitemap.xml): every published page

## Citation

When citing a day, cite its day page address, for example
https://www.crossingpersia.com/day-1.html. Say that the diary is a story told by a
fictional traveller, and cite the sources the day lists for any historical claim.
